about: The Pebble 2.0 loops on the page (src/lib/media.ts LaunchLoopId), cut from the launch film's own masters by tools/encode/loops.mjs: the film's pixels at its own 30 fps, never a new render. Frames are master frames (video/src/launch/master/timeline.ts: fr(slot.in) .. fr(slot.out)); `within` is the part of the scene clear of its seams (a zoom-through's settle, a whip's blur, a wipe) and of type that is entering or leaving. A loop plays `frames` frames: the source frames first .. first + frames, where the last `blend` of them dissolve into the first `blend` (source first + frames .. first + frames + blend into first .. first + blend), so the cycle closes on the film's own frames. It starts on `poster`, a telling frame, so the poster is the loop's frame 0 and the seam (last frame to first) is two neighbouring film frames. Each cut renders one file: `main` is loop-<id> (LAUNCH_LOOP_FRAMES), `phone` is loop-<id>-phone (LOOP_PHONE_FRAME, 1080 x 1350, the 4:5 master's own layout). Phase B (2 Nov 2026) checked every cycle against the final masters: each poster is a telling, still frame (its step from the frame before reads like the cycle's median, so verify.mjs's seam rule holds; mac, guard and stealth moved for it), and copy.ts media.launchLoops and CLAIMS C-LOOP2-* describe every frame of the delivered clips.

loops.label: The whole Mac with Pebble's window and the pebble, under “It lives on your Mac.” The desktop slides to another Space and the pebble stays: “On every Space.” A click opens the quick chat, and “What can you do now?” is sent: “Click. Ask.”

loops.note: S03's shots last 1.5 to 2 s each (Calculator 2.5-4.0, Calendar 4.0-6.0, Chrome 6.0-7.75, the window card 7.75-11.0), too short for a 6-10 s loop each: this one loop is the whole burst, under #mac's feature list as the section's one clip (the director's phase-B answer 1).
loops.label: “Now it can use your Mac.” In Calculator, Pebble keys in 48 × 12.5 and gets 600: “Your apps.” Calendar shows the new event Glaze order 09:00: “Your calendar.” Chrome shows Pebble's pill, “Pebble is working in this tab”: “Your browser.” Then Pebble's card asking to use one app window: “The app windows and websites you allow.”

A held reply: “Pebble's change isn't verified yet.” Under “Done means checked.”, Run the tests is pressed and the check reads “Verified · pytest 42 passed on current files”. Then “AgentGuard. Evidence before ‘done’.”, with three lines: “Tests the host ran, not the model’s word.” “Files you asked to keep, kept.” “Output matched to its file, byte for byte.”
loops.source: Pebble 2.0.1's own interface, run with sample data.

loops.label: “It builds small tools for itself.” A script makes the tool kiln_ramp_time. In a drawn diagram its own tests pass in a sandbox, a blind check passes 2 of 5, and the pebble asks. Pebble's card asks whether to keep the tool: “When the check disagrees, it asks you.”
loops.source: Recorded from Pebble 2.0.0, with a drawn diagram.

loops.label: “It remembers what matters.” A table of Pebble's six kinds of memory, then Settings › Memory: “All visible.” The pointer chooses Forget on one record, and it goes: “Forget anything.”
loops.source: Pebble 2.0.1's own interface, run with sample data.

loops.note: The scene's title stays at full size over the whole scene, and the page never shows that name (the owner's ruling, 2 Nov 2026): the clip is a 3:2 crop of the diagram alone. Measured on the final 16:9 master (2 Nov, phase B): the title's lowest glyphs reach y 220; the column spans y 258 (the over-budget box at its highest, about 15 frames) to 1030 (the last stub's border); the label "context budget" ends at x 775 at most (frames 1685 to 1710, when the camera's push is at its widest), so the crop starts at x 780 and runs to the frame's edge: 1140 x 760 from (780, 266), shown at that size, with no scaling. It leaves out every glyph of the title and of the label, keeps the dashed budget line, and trims at most 8 px of the over-budget box's top border for about 15 frames and 4 px of the last stub's lower border. No 4:5 cut: the 4:5 layout stacks the title over the diagram.
loops.label: Diagram. Six tool results stack up past a dashed line marked “context budget”. The three oldest are sealed into short stubs, the column falls back under the line, and one stub opens again, unchanged.

Pebble Remote on an iPhone screen, in the iOS Simulator: “Pebble, in your pocket.” “Pebble Remote for iPhone.” An edit waits for review; Apply Edit is tapped, the Face ID prompt passes, and the edit is done. “Approve with Face ID.” “Open source. Build it with Xcode.”
loops.source: Pebble Remote in the iOS Simulator, built from its published source, against a stand-in Mac.

loops.label: Pebble's ⌘K palette under “Presenting?”: “stealth” is typed and Turn Stealth Lockdown on is chosen. In a screen recording, Pebble's window leaves it as the setting turns on, and then the pebble wears the Veil. On screen: “Stealth Lockdown.” and its honest line.
loops.source: Recorded from Pebble 2.0.0; the Veil is a render by Pebble's own code.
